hints.title: Candidate Count Bounding
hints.text: At most two distinct elements can appear strictly more than one third of the time in any array. How can candidate pairs be maintained without sorting?

hints.title: Dual Voting Counter Invariant
hints.text: Extending the cancellation principle to two simultaneous candidates allows decrementing both candidate counts only when encountering a value different from both.

hints.title: Two Pass Boyer Moore Elimination Procedure
hints.text: Maintain two candidates and their respective counts. In the first pass, increment counts on match, initialize on zero count, or decrement both counts on complete mismatch. In a second pass, verify that the candidates appear strictly more than one third of the array length.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Sorting takes O(N log N) time, while storing full frequency counts in a dictionary consumes O(N) auxiliary space instead of O(1).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Boyer-Moore voting identifies at most two viable candidates in O(N) time and O(1) space, followed by an O(N) verification pass.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize the generalized Boyer-Moore threshold (k-1 candidates for > N/k) and remember the second confirmation pass.
